newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker on data, pare some losses.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker on data, pare some losses.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Friday, with prices pulled lower by stronger than expected U.S. and Canadian jobs data, but early losses pared by a firmer dollar and positive fiscal news, analysts said.

"The improving dollar probably helps the sentiment a little bit. Also, I think the latest deficit news helped as well," said Mary Jane Yule, a senior portfolio manager with Jones Heward Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$1.05 to C$107.50 to yield 7.351 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1-8/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 50 basis points from 54 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
Canadian bonds opened weaker on Friday after a Statistics Canada report showed Canadian employment grew by a slightly greater than expected 34,000 jobs in December.
But Canadian bonds tumbled further with U.S. treasuries after the U.S. Labor Department reported the U.S. economy created a higher than expected 262,000 jobs in December.
Canadian bonds pared losses near the end of the session, helped by a stronger currency.
The dollar firmed to C$1.3485 (US$0.7416) from Thursday's close at C$1.3521 (US$0.7396) in fairly heavy trading, helped by buying from U.S. investment firms.
In fiscal news, the Finance Department reported that for the fiscal year to date, April to November, the deficit totaled C$8.12 billion, down from C$19.26 billion a year earlier.
The sharp jump in yields on bonds early in the session also lured many buyers into the market, helping prices to rebound partly, Yule said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.45 to C$102.05 to yield 6.711 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 25/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 10 basis points from 17 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.91 percent against the U.S. bill, which yielded 5.16 percent.
